content:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. In my current role at Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and merge-request environments used by three product teams, supporting the delivery and testing of services through reliable, repeatable infrastructure workflows. I’m looking to build on this experience in a platform and infrastructure engineering role, and Corvale’s work connecting a new train fleet with cloud services makes this opportunity particularly compelling.

I’ve improved CI pipelines across three teams, reducing average run time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly runner costs by about 30%. I also delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments deployed with Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster, with automated cleanup and end-to-end testing. These projects have strengthened my analytical approach to infrastructure reliability and my ability to coordinate practical changes across product teams. I wrote Odrava’s internal guide to how CI works, which is used in onboarding, and mentored two QA interns.

My hands-on infrastructure experience includes Docker, Helm, GitLab CI, and namespace-level Kubernetes work. Outside work, I built a three-node k3s homelab with GitOps deployments, monitoring, ingress and TLS certificate management, and provisioned a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform. My Terraform experience is currently from personal projects; I’m continuing to develop my infrastructure-as-code skills. I would bring a solid foundation in automation, observability and test infrastructure, alongside a clear understanding of the scope I’m ready to grow into.

Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on teams owning systems and solving problems collaboratively resonate with how I’ve approached improving shared CI and test environments. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support the Fleet Connectivity team as it shapes reliable, observable infrastructure for the new fleet.

Thank you for your consideration.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional and well-structured cover letter with strong use of quantified achievements. It effectively connects the candidate’s CI/CD, ephemeral-environment, Kubernetes and observability experience to Corvale’s infrastructure work. The explanation of Terraform as personal-project experience is appropriately transparent. The main weakness is that the letter presents relevant implementation experience but does not explicitly frame it as systems design, infrastructure operation, technical leadership, or stakeholder alignment in the terminology used by the advertisement. It also spends some space emphasizing the candidate’s transition and development areas, which slightly undersells the value already demonstrated.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard paragraphs, contains no problematic tables or graphics, and includes relevant searchable terms such as GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitOps, monitoring, ingress, TLS certificate management, automation and observability. AI screening probability is moderate to good for an adjacent or junior/mid-level DevOps profile, but weaker for this specific contractor role because the letter does not mention AWS, Linux, infrastructure-as-code, cloud environment operation, systems architecture, stakeholder leadership, or secure networking in the employer’s terminology. It correctly does not claim unsupported Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud ownership, or production Kubernetes administration.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role’s analytical thinking, communication, automation, observability, reliability and collaborative-working expectations. The candidate has credible hands-on infrastructure-adjacent experience through GitLab CI ownership, merge-request environments, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, a k3s/GitOps homelab, monitoring, TLS certificate management and personal Terraform work. The candidate’s material does not support strong Terraform and Terragrunt experience, mTLS expertise, IoT or remote-device integration, broad cloud environment operation, or production-level infrastructure ownership; these are genuine profile gaps rather than cover-letter defects. AWS is present only through personal free-tier learning and is not currently shown in the letter. The letter should make the strongest truthful connections to system design, infrastructure-as-code, technical coordination and cloud fundamentals without overstating seniority or operational scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the second paragraph, make the systems-design content more explicit by changing the sentence beginning “I also delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments...” to describe the design and operational workflow. For example: “I designed and delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments for each merge request, with seeded data, Helm-based deployment to a shared Kubernetes cluster, end-to-end test execution and automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.” This remains supported by the candidate’s project information and better matches the requirement for systems architecture and system design.

2. In the third paragraph, replace the broad sentence “My hands-on infrastructure experience includes Docker, Helm, GitLab CI, and namespace-level Kubernetes work” with a more ATS-aligned but accurate description: “My hands-on infrastructure engineering experience includes GitLab CI, Docker, Helm-based Kubernetes deployments, namespace-level operation of shared environments, and infrastructure-as-code practice with Terraform.” Do not describe the candidate as operating the Kubernetes cluster itself, since the original information says the platform team owns the cluster.

3. In the third paragraph, add the supported AWS fundamentals so the letter does not omit a preferred qualification. After the Terraform sentence, add: “I have also used AWS EC2 and S3 at a fundamentals level through personal free-tier projects.” Keep the wording limited to personal learning and do not imply professional AWS ownership.

4. In the second paragraph, strengthen the technical-leadership and stakeholder evidence by changing “These projects have strengthened my analytical approach to infrastructure reliability and my ability to coordinate practical changes across product teams” to: “These projects required profiling systems, proposing and coordinating changes across three product teams, and bringing developers and QA stakeholders along through clearer CI documentation and visibility into flaky tests.” This is supported by the candidate’s pipeline work, internal CI guide and dashboard project and better addresses the requirement to lead technical topics and bring stakeholders along.

5. In the third paragraph, add Linux, which is supported by the original candidate information and is relevant to the nice-to-have requirements. For example, revise the opening of that paragraph to: “My hands-on infrastructure engineering experience includes Linux-based development and test environments, Docker, Helm, GitLab CI...” Do not add virtual-machine experience, because it is not supported by the candidate information.

MINOR REFINEMENT
6. In the final sentence of the third paragraph, replace “I’m continuing to develop my infrastructure-as-code skills” with a less self-undermining formulation that remains truthful: “This has given me a practical foundation in infrastructure-as-code, automation, observability and test infrastructure, while my Terraform experience to date has been through personal projects.” This preserves the important limitation without making the candidate sound less capable than the evidence supports.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, focused, and well structured. It presents credible quantified achievements, explains the transition from QA automation toward DevOps/platform engineering, and maintains appropriate transparency about Terraform and AWS being personal-project experience. The examples are relevant to CI/CD, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, reliability, analytical problem solving, and stakeholder communication. The letter is slightly dense in the third paragraph, but overall it is persuasive and substantially tailored to Corvale's Fleet Connectivity context. No unsupported skills or experiences were identified when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses clear headings-free prose, standard paragraph formatting, and searchable terms including GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Linux, PostgreSQL, infrastructure-as-code, observability, and TLS certificate management. Its ATS and AI-screening probability is moderate to good for the documented experience, but it will not strongly match several exact requirements because the candidate's source material does not support Terragrunt, mTLS, networking design, or strong cloud infrastructure experience. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than document defects. The wording around Kubernetes is appropriately qualified by referring to namespace-level operation and shared environments, avoiding overstatement.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with hands-on infrastructure workflows, CI/CD ownership, Kubernetes test environments, infrastructure-as-code practice, observability, reliability improvement, analytical thinking, clear communication, and leading changes across three product teams. It also shows AWS exposure at the fundamentals level and Linux experience. The candidate's material does not demonstrate strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS or broader networking knowledge, full cloud environment operation in a professional setting, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, or backend/full-stack experience. The material also does not establish a strong systems-architecture/system-design background or virtual-machine experience. These are genuine role-alignment gaps and should not be implied as qualifications in the letter. The cultural alignment is credible through references to collaborative ownership, cross-team improvement, and Corvale's engineering-led approach.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the second paragraph, make the technical leadership evidence slightly more explicit by changing "These projects required profiling systems, proposing and coordinating changes across three product teams, and bringing developers and QA stakeholders along through clearer CI documentation and visibility into flaky tests" to "These projects required analysing system bottlenecks, leading technical proposals across three product teams, coordinating implementation, and bringing developers and QA stakeholders along through clearer CI documentation and flaky-test visibility." This uses the job description's "leading technical proposals" language while remaining supported by the documented pipeline profiling, coordination, documentation, and stakeholder work.
